newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends higher on cash market, N.Korea news.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends higher on cash market, N.Korea news.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended higher Monday in response to continued cash market strength and news of authorization of a food deal between Cargill and North Korea, pit traders said.
"We're approaching the summer highs, and everybody's bullish on the cash market," said a pit trader.
Cash market prices were said to be firm, and farmers were said to be reluctant sellers as they wait for prices to move even higher, traders said.
The May and July contracts both set fresh contract highs Monday.
News that Cargill was granted approval by the U.S. Treasure to sell up to 500,000 tonnes of wheat or rice to N. Korea was seen as supportive, traders said.
"It's the tonnage that is important to the market," a pit trader said.
Rice volume was estimated 600 contracts, down from 814 on Friday, according to CBOT data.
Rice closed 0.01 to 13 cents per cwt higher, with January up 13 at $11.10 and March up eight cents at $11.21.
